paragraphs: AstroVisBench evaluates whether language models can help with astronomy research by processing data and producing scientifically meaningful visualizations. The motivation is that useful scientific computation involves more than generating code: the resulting analysis and plots must convey the right patterns. The benchmark brings these connected responsibilities into one evaluation.

It tests two abilities: constructing astronomy-specific data analysis workflows and turning their results into complex plots. To assess the visualizations, the authors introduce a workflow in which a language model acts as a judge. They validate this judging process against annotations from five professional astronomers, connecting automated assessment with domain expertise.

The evaluation of leading language models reveals a substantial gap in their usefulness as astronomy research assistants. This finding concerns the full route from data processing to visual communication, where outputs must support scientific interpretation. The broader contribution is an evaluation approach for visualization-centered scientific workflows, with potential relevance to fields such as physics and biology.
neurips-2025-astrovisbench-a-code-benchm.tldr: AstroVisBench tests astronomy analysis and visualization workflows, revealing substantial gaps in current language models’ usefulness as scientific assistants.

paragraphs: AugGen investigates whether carefully generated training examples can improve face recognition while reducing dependence on large collections of real images. The paper motivates this direction through privacy and ethical concerns surrounding such datasets. Its central design choice is to build the augmentation process entirely around the target face recognition dataset.

The method trains a class-conditional generative model exclusively on that dataset, then strategically samples synthetic examples from it. This makes the augmentation self-contained: it does not require external datasets or pretrained models. The approach emphasizes how generated data are selected and integrated into recognition training, rather than relying on additional outside resources.

Across eight face recognition benchmarks, including IJB-C and IJB-B, the authors report improvements of 1–12%. AugGen outperforms training on real data alone and the compared leading synthetic generation approaches while using less real data. The gains often exceed those from architectural changes, supporting synthetic augmentation as a useful option in data-limited settings. The stated privacy benefit is mitigation of constraints, rather than a formal privacy guarantee.
neurips-2025-auggen-synthetic-augmentati.tldr: AugGen generates augmentation data using only the target face dataset, improving recognition across eight benchmarks while using less real data.

paragraphs: CLAMP approaches self-supervised visual learning as a geometric packing problem. Its inspiration comes from neural manifolds: structures formed by neuronal responses to different stimulus classes. If representations of different categories occupy well-separated structures, classification becomes easier. The paper uses this perspective to move beyond contrastive learning organized around individual point comparisons.

Multiple augmented views of one image form a sub-manifold in the learned representation space. A packing loss adjusts both the sizes and positions of these structures. The loss draws inspiration from the potential energy of particles with short-range repulsion, giving the learning dynamics a connection to packing and jamming physics and making its hyperparameters geometrically interpretable.

Under linear evaluation, where the learned backbone stays fixed and only a linear classifier is trained, CLAMP performs competitively with leading self-supervised methods. The authors also observe that category-level manifolds emerge naturally and become separated. These findings support manifold packing as a useful representation-learning framework while offering a geometric account of how the learned space becomes organized.
neurips-2025-contrastive-self-supervised.tldr: CLAMP learns visual representations by packing and separating geometric structures, achieving competitive self-supervised performance with interpretable learning dynamics.

paragraphs: This paper studies control problems in which a system evolves continuously, is affected by randomness, and can also undergo abrupt jumps. Decisions must be chosen over a finite time horizon. The proposed approach uses a model of these dynamics to train neural networks that represent the decision rule and its associated value.

The method iteratively trains two networks with complementary roles. One represents the optimal policy, while the other approximates the value function used to assess decisions. The authors derive two training objectives from the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation through a continuous-time dynamic programming principle. This connects the learning objectives to the stochastic dynamics of the control problem.

Empirical evaluations on several problems illustrate the method’s accuracy and scalability, including its ability to address complex, high-dimensional tasks. The contribution is a model-based training framework that links policy learning and value approximation through continuous-time control theory. The reported findings provide evidence that this framework can be effective for the evaluated problems involving random evolution and jumps.
neurips-2025-deep-learning-for-continuou.tldr: A model-based neural approach jointly learns policies and value functions for finite-horizon continuous-time control problems with randomness and jumps.

paragraphs: Disentangled representation learning aims to separate factors of variation in data. Existing approaches often build factor-specific assumptions into their architectures or training objectives, making adaptation cumbersome when different factors coexist. This paper instead places the relevant assumptions in a modular rule for recombining latent representations.

The key observation is that factors follow different recombination rules. Global attributes involve mutually exclusive alternatives, whereas different objects can coexist in subsets. The method randomly mixes latent components according to the desired rules, then applies two objectives. A prior loss encourages each remix to decode into a realistic image, and a compositional consistency loss aligns that image with its mixed latent representation.

Changing the mixing strategy lets the same framework target attributes, objects, or both without redesigning its architecture or objectives. Experiments show competitive performance for attribute and object disentanglement, and the authors report a distinctive ability to jointly disentangle global style and objects. The approach therefore makes the choice of recombination rules the central way to express which factor structure the model should discover.
neurips-2025-disentangled-representation.tldr: A modular latent-mixing strategy enables attribute, object, and joint disentanglement without changing the model architecture or training objectives.

paragraphs: Bisimulation metrics measure similarity between stochastic processes, including Markov chains. Earlier computational methods require full knowledge of the transition dynamics, meaning the probabilities governing movement between states must be available. This paper targets a more practical situation: observations arrive as sample trajectories, without an explicit transition model.

The authors develop a new linear programming formulation of these metrics and solve it using stochastic primal-dual optimization. This provides a way to estimate the distance through sample access. The approach builds on the connection between bisimulation metrics and optimal transport while changing the information needed to carry out the computation.

The paper supplies theoretical sample-complexity guarantees and evaluates the algorithm empirically. Together, these contributions address both the amount of sampled information required and the method’s observed effectiveness. Its significance is the shift from comparing fully specified transition models to estimating process similarity from sampled behavior, making this class of metrics applicable in settings where the dynamics cannot be supplied explicitly.
neurips-2025-distances-for-markov-chains.tldr: A stochastic optimization method estimates bisimulation distances between Markov chains from samples without requiring explicit transition models.

paragraphs: EOC-Bench evaluates how multimodal language models understand objects in changing, first-person environments. Such understanding must persist as people interact with tools and other objects in cluttered scenes. The paper argues that benchmarks centered on static appearance and spatial properties do not adequately assess the changes produced by these interactions.

The benchmark contains 3,277 annotated question–answer pairs organized around the past, present, and future. It covers 11 detailed evaluation dimensions and three visual ways of referring to objects. A mixed-format annotation framework with human involvement supports this assessment, allowing object understanding to be examined across multiple temporal perspectives rather than a single static view.

The authors evaluate proprietary models, open-source models, and models designed around object-level processing. The contribution described in the abstract is a systematic testing resource for identifying, recalling, and forecasting objects in dynamic egocentric scenarios. By organizing evaluation around objects and time, it provides a basis for studying the persistent contextual understanding needed by embodied systems.
neurips-2025-eoc-bench-can-mllms-identif.tldr: EOC-Bench tests multimodal models’ ability to understand objects across past, present, and future in dynamic first-person scenes.

paragraphs: SADis addresses a specific customization problem in stylized text-to-image generation: controlling color and texture independently using separate reference images. Existing diffusion methods can capture styles from a few examples, but controlling their individual attributes remains difficult. The proposed approach separates these attributes without requiring model tuning.

The method uses an additivity property of image prompts in CLIP’s embedding space to extract distinct color and texture representations. It then applies a whitening and coloring transformation to bring the generated palette closer to the color reference. Because this process can lose texture through a bias associated with diffusion training, the authors add a noise term to preserve textural fidelity.

These components form a regularized transformation that supports separate control of the two style attributes. On images from WikiArt and StyleDrop, the authors report qualitative and quantitative improvements over leading stylization methods for the disentangled generation task. The findings support the usefulness of combining separated style embeddings with a color adjustment procedure that explicitly protects texture.
neurips-2025-free-lunch-color-texture-di.tldr: SADis separates color and texture control in stylized image generation through reference embeddings and a texture-preserving color transformation, without model tuning.

paragraphs: Policy World Model connects driving scene prediction with trajectory planning. The paper starts from the observation that world models are often trained to simulate future scenes separately from choosing a driving trajectory. Its goal is to make learned knowledge about how the world evolves directly useful for planning.

PWM places world modeling and planning in one architecture and introduces action-free future-state forecasting. Through collaborative prediction of states and actions, the framework uses anticipation of future conditions to support planning. To make video forecasting more efficient, it also generates tokens in parallel, using a context-guided tokenizer and an adaptive dynamic focal loss.

The authors report that PWM matches or exceeds leading approaches using multiple camera views or multiple input modalities, despite relying only on a front camera. This result supports their proposed connection between forecasting and planning in the evaluated setting. The contribution combines an architectural integration with a specific forecasting mechanism intended to help world knowledge improve trajectory decisions, alongside changes that support efficient video prediction.
neurips-2025-from-forecasting-to-plannin.tldr: Policy World Model integrates future-state forecasting and driving trajectory planning, reporting strong performance using only front-camera input.

paragraphs: State space layers can handle long-range sequence tasks, but reducing their size after training can be difficult. This paper tackles that problem during training by encouraging a structure that is easier to compress later. Its regularization target is the sum of the layer’s Hankel singular values.

The approach uses the relationship between rapidly decaying Hankel singular values and compressibility. Penalizing their sum encourages that decay, preparing the trained state space model for compression. To make this practical during repeated training updates, the authors develop an efficient computation algorithm that exploits the block-diagonal system matrices used in their chosen parameterization.

Experiments on Long Range Arena show that the regularized state space layers can be up to ten times more compressible than standard state space layers while retaining high accuracy. The result concerns compressibility rather than a reported tenfold acceleration of the entire network. The broader idea is to make eventual compression part of the training objective, supported by a computation strategy tailored to the model’s matrix structure.
neurips-2025-hankel-singular-value-regul.tldr: Regularizing Hankel singular values during training makes state space layers up to ten times more compressible while maintaining high accuracy.

paragraphs: This paper addresses uncertainty in image super-resolution produced by generative models. Its proposed output is a confidence mask that communicates where the restored image can be trusted. The aim is to make uncertainty local and interpretable, so confidence is tied to particular image regions rather than treated only as an overall property.

The method uses conformal prediction and calibration data to construct the mask. It can work with any black-box generative model, including one accessible only through an opaque API. Users can customize it through a local image similarity metric, which determines how fidelity is assessed. This makes the meaning of the mask depend explicitly on the chosen comparison criterion.

The authors prove guarantees covering fidelity error control under that metric, reconstruction quality, and robustness to data leakage. They also evaluate the method empirically and report solid performance. The contribution is a way to attach theoretically supported uncertainty information to generated restorations without needing access to the underlying model’s internal implementation.
neurips-2025-image-super-resolution-with.tldr: Conformal prediction produces local confidence masks for black-box super-resolution models, with guarantees tied to a chosen image similarity metric.

paragraphs: AI-generated content expands the range of treatments available in digital experiments, but makes those treatments difficult to represent analytically. A treatment can contain rich semantic information that is lost by an overly simple encoding. This paper learns compact representations intended to retain useful structure while making causal analysis manageable.

The proposed double kernel representation learning method represents both treatments and user covariates. It models the causal effect through an inner product between these kernel-based representations. An alternating-minimization algorithm learns them from data, and the authors establish convergence guarantees under a low-rank factor model. That model is the stated condition supporting the convergence result.

The representations can support generating meaningful treatment variants and choosing treatment assignments adaptively during online experiments. The paper develops an adaptive experimental design strategy as a concrete application and demonstrates effectiveness through numerical experiments. Its contribution links semantic treatment structure with causal effect modeling, giving the learned representations a role in both analyzing experiments and guiding subsequent experimentation.
neurips-2025-leveraging-semantic-similar.tldr: Double kernel representation learning compresses rich treatments and user characteristics into representations that support causal effect modeling and adaptive experimentation.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can emulate dynamical systems, but their inference cost makes fast physics emulation difficult. This paper investigates an approach already used in image and video generation: performing generation in an autoencoder’s compressed latent space. The central question is how well this compression preserves the accuracy needed for dynamical-system emulation.

The empirical study finds that emulation accuracy remains surprisingly robust across a broad range of compression rates, reaching up to 1,000 times compression. This suggests that, in the studied settings, a much smaller representation can still retain information useful for emulation. The compression figure describes representation compression, rather than a stated equivalent increase in runtime speed.

The authors also find diffusion-based emulators consistently more accurate than the non-generative alternatives they evaluate. When predictions are uncertain, the generative models compensate with greater diversity. Alongside these findings, the paper discusses architecture and optimizer choices that proved important for training latent-space emulators, connecting its empirical conclusions to practical decisions involved in constructing such systems.
neurips-2025-lost-in-latent-space-an-emp.tldr: An empirical study finds latent diffusion physics emulators retain accuracy across compression rates up to 1,000 times and outperform evaluated non-generative alternatives.

paragraphs: Omni3D reconstructs a scene for omnidirectional rendering from a single image. The paper addresses a difficulty in diffusion-based reconstruction: generated views can contain geometric distortions or disagree with one another. These inconsistencies make it harder to recover a coherent three-dimensional scene from the collection of generated images.

The method uses priors from pose estimation techniques such as MASt3R and repeatedly refines both the generated views and their estimated camera poses. It adjusts images to reduce three-dimensional reprojection errors between paired views, then corrects pose estimates using the refined images. This joint process lets improvements in image consistency and camera estimation support one another.

The resulting views and poses are used to construct an explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting representation that supports omnidirectional rendering. Experiments show substantially improved reconstruction quality compared with previous leading methods. The main contribution is the coordinated refinement step: it makes diffusion-generated views more geometrically compatible before they are assembled into the final scene representation.
neurips-2025-omnidirectional-3d-scene-re.tldr: Omni3D jointly refines generated views and camera poses to improve single-image reconstruction for omnidirectional 3D rendering.

paragraphs: Quantum state tomography concerns learning an unknown quantum state. In standard settings, pure states are substantially easier to learn than general mixed states. This paper asks whether that advantage survives when learning takes place online, and proves that the two classes have the same regret scaling in this setting.

The central result compares their sequential fat-shattering dimensions, a complexity measure relevant to online learning. The authors show that these dimensions are almost the same for pure and mixed states, which leads to identical regret scaling. The distinction between the state classes therefore does not produce the usual learning advantage under this online criterion.

The paper also extends earlier online tomography results in two directions: an epsilon-realizable setting and partial learning of the density matrix using smoothed analysis. These extensions broaden the learning settings addressed by the theory. Overall, the work demonstrates that the relative difficulty of pure and mixed state learning depends on the learning framework, with online learning exhibiting a different relationship from standard tomography.
neurips-2025-online-learning-of-pure-sta.tldr: Pure and mixed quantum states have nearly the same sequential complexity and identical regret scaling in online learning.

paragraphs: TOT studies online forecasting when hidden variables change the relationship between past and future observations. These latent influences can produce unknown distribution shifts over time. The framework aims to make them useful to a forecaster, combining a theoretical account of their value with a model-agnostic approach to incorporating them.

The authors prove that providing latent variables tightens the Bayes risk. The benefit persists when those variables are estimated with uncertainty and increases when they are more precisely identifiable. They further propose identifying latent variables from minimal adjacent observations. These results connect forecasting performance to how well the hidden factors can be recovered.

The implementation blueprint uses a temporal decoder to match the observed-variable distribution and two separate noise estimators for latent causal inference and observed-variable mixing. Synthetic experiments support the theoretical claims. Plug-in implementations across several forecasting baselines also produce general improvements on multiple benchmarks, providing empirical support for adding latent-variable modeling to existing online forecasters.
neurips-2025-online-time-series-forecast.tldr: TOT combines theory and a model-agnostic design to improve online forecasting by identifying latent factors behind changing data distributions.

paragraphs: ReCon-GS reconstructs changing scenes online while accounting for the memory needed to store them. It represents motion through multiple levels of Anchor Gaussians, allocated adaptively according to density. This breaks geometric changes between frames into a compact hierarchy ranging from coarse motion to finer local deformation.

The hierarchy can be reorganized on demand to retain expressive local motion. Deformation information is inherited within the appropriate hierarchy levels to preserve temporal consistency. A storage-aware optimization mechanism also adjusts anchor density at different levels, giving control over the trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and memory use while supporting real-time rendering.

Across three datasets, the authors report approximately 15% better training efficiency than leading methods, alongside improved free-viewpoint video synthesis quality, robustness, and stability. At equivalent rendering quality, memory requirements fall by more than 50%. These results support the combination of adaptive motion hierarchy and storage-aware optimization as a way to make dynamic reconstruction more compact without sacrificing the reported rendering quality.
neurips-2025-recon-gs-continuum-preserve.tldr: ReCon-GS uses adaptive Gaussian motion hierarchies to improve dynamic reconstruction efficiency and reduce memory by over 50% at equivalent rendering quality.

paragraphs: OHSVGP is an online Gaussian process model designed to retain long-term information from sequential data. It incorporates HiPPO, a framework associated with long-range memory in recurrent neural networks. The paper’s central move is to reinterpret HiPPO’s evolving projections as components of a sparse variational Gaussian process.

Specifically, the method treats time-varying orthogonal projections as inducing variables built from time-dependent polynomial basis functions. These variables summarize process history within the interdomain Gaussian process framework. The authors also show that kernel matrices can be updated recurrently using the differential-equation evolution of HiPPO, connecting the memory representation to an online computation procedure.

Evaluation covers one-dimensional time-series prediction, continual discriminative learning with multidimensional inputs, and deep generative modeling through a sparse Gaussian process variational autoencoder. Across these settings, the authors report improvements over existing online Gaussian process methods in prediction, preservation of long-term memory, and computational efficiency. The results support bringing structured recurrent memory into probabilistic models that update as data arrive.
neurips-2025-recurrent-memory-for-online.tldr: OHSVGP incorporates recurrent HiPPO memory into online Gaussian processes, improving prediction, historical memory, and computational efficiency in the evaluated settings.

paragraphs: This paper targets object–context shortcuts in vision-language models: predictions can depend too heavily on familiar backgrounds rather than the object itself. Such shortcuts undermine zero-shot recognition when test scenes differ from training co-occurrences. The method asks whether a prediction would persist if the same object appeared in a different environment.

At inference time, it estimates object and background expectations in CLIP’s representation space. It then constructs counterfactual embeddings by combining object features with alternative contexts from external datasets, neighboring batch examples, or text descriptions. Using a Total Direct Effect estimate and simulated intervention, it subtracts background-only activation while preserving useful interactions between objects and their surroundings.

The method requires neither retraining nor prompt design. On context-sensitive benchmarks, the authors report substantial improvements in both average and worst-group accuracy, reaching a new zero-shot state of the art. The contribution is a lightweight representation-level calibration procedure that uses counterfactual context changes to reduce misleading scores associated with background shortcuts.
neurips-2025-representation-level-counte.tldr: Counterfactual recombination of object and context embeddings improves zero-shot recognition by reducing background-driven scores without retraining.

paragraphs: SwapGT studies how graph Transformers build token sequences for node classification. These sequences determine which graph information reaches the Transformer. The authors observe that existing methods focus on immediate neighbors in constructed similarity graphs, restricting the nodes used to create diverse sequences and limiting the resulting representations.

The proposed method introduces token swapping to use semantic relationships among nodes more fully. This operation produces more informative token sequences, which a Transformer backbone then converts into node representations. A center alignment loss adds a constraint across representations learned from multiple sequences, tying the sequence-generation mechanism to the representation-learning objective.

Experiments across various datasets show that SwapGT outperforms the compared approaches for node classification. The findings emphasize that the construction of Transformer inputs is a consequential part of graph learning. Here, improving the diversity and semantic relevance of those inputs, together with aligning the resulting representations, provides the route to stronger classification performance.
neurips-2025-rethinking-tokenized-graph-.tldr: SwapGT improves node classification through semantically informed token swapping and alignment of representations learned from multiple token sequences.

paragraphs: This work addresses a data bottleneck in reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning: studying broader capabilities requires high-quality examples from multiple domains. The authors introduce a 92,000-example dataset spanning mathematics, code, science, logic, simulation, and tabular reasoning. Each domain includes verifiers to support reinforcement-learning feedback.

The curation pipeline includes sourcing, deduplication, reward design, and filtering tailored to domain and difficulty. This creates a resource for examining how reinforcement learning transfers across reasoning domains. The study suggests that a simple mixture of domains can be effective and identifies factors affecting transferability, making cross-domain behavior a central focus of the investigation.

The authors train 7B and 32B models purely through reinforcement learning on the curated data. On a 17-task evaluation covering six domains, they report gains of 7.3% and 7.8%, respectively, over leading open reinforcement-learning reasoning baselines. The results support the value of carefully curated mixed-domain training, and the planned dataset, code, and evaluation release is intended to enable further investigation.
neurips-2025-revisiting-reinforcement-le.tldr: A curated six-domain reasoning dataset supports mixed-domain reinforcement learning and yields reported improvements for both 7B and 32B models.

paragraphs: Masked diffusion models allow tokens to be generated in different orders and in parallel, offering flexibility beyond sequential generation. Their training is complicated by the fact that predicting a token can become easier or harder depending on which other positions are already visible. SPMDM addresses this variation through a more structured sampling path.

The paper identifies two useful characteristics: favoring tokens close to already unmasked tokens and generating subsequences earlier in reasoning. It divides sequences into fixed-length, non-overlapping subsequences and applies different noise scales. This design is intended to teach both dependencies among individual tokens and dependencies across the larger subsequence units.

On synthetic data and tasks including Countdown and Sudoku, SPMDM captures structural rules effectively and significantly outperforms the evaluated masked diffusion and autoregressive models. It also achieves competitive results on broader reasoning benchmarks. The findings support structuring the generation path as a way to make masked diffusion learning more effective, with the strongest reported advantages appearing in the stated structured tasks.
neurips-2025-spmdm-enhancing-masked-diff.tldr: SPMDM structures masked diffusion generation around fixed-length subsequences, improving rule learning and performance on tasks including Countdown and Sudoku.

paragraphs: CameraBench evaluates how well people and models understand camera movement in video. It contains roughly 3,000 diverse internet videos with expert annotations checked through multiple quality-control stages. A central contribution is a vocabulary of camera-motion primitives developed with cinematographers, covering movements that depend on geometry as well as scene meaning.

These distinctions matter because visually similar effects can arise differently. Zooming changes camera intrinsics, whereas moving forward changes extrinsics; novices can learn to distinguish them through tutorials. Other labels, such as following a subject, require understanding what is moving in the scene. The human study finds that expertise and tutorial-based training can significantly improve accuracy.

Model evaluations reveal complementary weaknesses. Structure-from-Motion systems struggle with content-dependent semantic motions, while generative video-language models struggle with motions requiring precise trajectory estimation. The authors fine-tune a generative video-language model on CameraBench to better combine these abilities, and demonstrate uses in motion-aware captions, video question answering, and video–text retrieval.
neurips-2025-towards-understanding-camer.tldr: CameraBench combines expert-labeled videos and a camera-motion vocabulary to reveal and improve geometric and semantic motion understanding.

paragraphs: Diff-Spectra reconstructs hyperspectral information from RGB images while addressing metamerism: different underlying spectra can produce nearly identical RGB values. This ambiguity makes reliable reconstruction difficult. The approach combines supervised, physics-aware estimation with unsupervised regularization intended to keep reconstructed spectra consistent with the statistical properties of real hyperspectral data.

An Adaptive illumiChroma Decoupling module separates illumination and chrominance information to learn more distinctive features. It is incorporated into an initial estimator guided by a learnable spectral response function, connecting the network to physical image formation. These constraints make the reconstruction task more interpretable and help mitigate the ambiguity associated with metamerism.

The authors also generate augmented metameric spectra to pretrain a spectral diffusion module. During inference, this module regularizes spectral transitions through an inner optimization loop. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance for both spectral reconstruction and downstream hyperspectral classification. The contribution therefore joins physical constraints and learned spectral statistics, with reported benefits extending from reconstructed spectra to a subsequent recognition task.
neurips-2025-unraveling-metameric-dilemm.tldr: Diff-Spectra combines physics-aware estimation and diffusion-based regularization to mitigate RGB spectral ambiguity and improve hyperspectral reconstruction and classification.

paragraphs: VL-SAM-V2 addresses discovering objects beyond a detector’s familiar categories. Open-set systems accept user-provided category names at inference time, while open-ended systems aim to discover unseen objects without that input. The paper seeks to combine the stronger performance of open-set approaches with the autonomous discovery capability of open-ended approaches.

Its framework brings queries from both kinds of models into a general and specific query fusion module, where they can interact. Adjusting the open-set queries allows evaluation in either mode. Ranked learnable queries are matched by sorting to proposals from open-ended models, encouraging more diverse queries, and a denoising point strategy supports training.

On LVIS, the authors report improvements over previous open-set and open-ended methods, with particularly strong gains on rare objects. These findings support query interaction as a useful mechanism for combining category-directed detection with broader discovery. The framework’s contribution is both its fusion mechanism and its ability to operate with or without category-level human input at inference.
neurips-2025-vl-sam-v2-open-world-object.tldr: VL-SAM-V2 fuses open-set and open-ended detection queries, improving LVIS performance especially for rare objects while supporting both inference modes.
